FACILITY DESCRIPTION The Discharger owns and operates a wastewater collection, treatment, and disposal system (Facility) that provides sewerage service to the Coachella Valley; City of La Quinta, Mecca, Palm Desert, and Thousand Palms with a service population of approximately 63,000. The wastewater treatment plant has a treatment (design) capacity of 9.9 million gallons per day (MGD) and is located in the Sections 2, T17S, R8E, SBB&M26. 2.A. Discharge of Wastewater Treatment and Controls The Facility consists of two treatment systems running in parallel: a lagoon treatment system rated at 7.0 million gallons per day (MGD) and a Biolac® activated sludge treatment system rated at 2.9 MGD. The headworks system two automatic bar screens, conveyor, two grinder-washer compactors, a grit channel, grit pump, grit cyclone separator, and influent pump dry well with three influent pumps. All headworks buildings are equipped with fresh air ventilation and foul air odor scrubbers. The influent flow from the headworks is distributed to five treatment modules. chunks.text: The primary stage of wastewater treatment is the removal of both grit and primary sludge. Grit is represented in the model as solid-state silicon dioxide which is about 1% of the total inlet water flow. The grit in wastewater has a specific gravity in the range 1.5-2.7 kg/l which is much higher than that of the organic matter suspended in the influent stream (1.02 kg/l). A differential sedimentation can thus be a successful mechanism for separating grit from organic matter (Liu and Lipták, 2000) . A density-based classifier is defined as a unit operation to remove the grit in this model. The primary treatment can reduce the Total Suspended Solids (TSS) by 50-60%. Also, it implies the removal of the BOD in the incoming wastewater by 20-30%. The percentage of the sludge removal chosen in the present model is 55%.

chunks.text: A pilot-scale system, consisting of a grit tank and microscreen for primary treatment followed by a SAF-MBR 2.0 for secondary treatment, was installed at the Codiga Resource Recovery Center (Stanford, CA), as illustrated in. The pilot-scale system treated municipal wastewater pumped from the Serra Street sewer on the Stanford campus for more than three years. Sewage was de-gritted in a grit tank then subject to primary treatment by screening through a 0.3 mm pore size microscreen (MS-28, Hydro International). The pilot-scale SAF-MBR 2.0 consisted of: (1) two AFBRs operated in parallel, hereafter referred to as AFBR 1 and AFBR 2, containing fluidized GAC biocarrier, and (2) a gas-sparged membrane tank equipped with ultrafiltration membranes. Recirculation of bulk fluid (twice the influent flow rate) between the three reactors enabled complete mixing and control of solids accumulation within the gas-sparged membrane tank.

chunks.text: 2.1. Process Layout. The facility of the present study is located in the southwestern United States in an area characterized by a semi-arid coastal climate. The secondary process includes an activated sludge process operating in the Ludzack-Ettinger configuration with an annual average SRT of 5 days. The aeration tank has six zones in series with seven in EPDM membrane disc diffusers. The process is operated in a step-feed mode with a 60/40 split between the first and third zones, which are operated under anoxic conditions using coarse-bubble diffusers and mechanical mixers, respectively, and no nitrite/nitrate recirculation. Furthermore, information about the facility structure and wastewater characteristics is reported in the Supporting Information, §1. 2.2. Sensors Installed.

chunks.text: Preliminary treatment is the initial stage where coarse particles and foreign matter commonly found in raw wastewater are removed to optimize subsequent treatment processes (Sonune and Ghate, 2004) . This stage involves activities such as coarse screening, grit removal, and the comminution of large objects in wastewater. Grit chambers maintain high water velocities, preventing organic compounds from settling within the chamber. Although not all wastewater treatment plants incorporate grit removal in their preliminary treatment, some employ comminutors alongside coarse screening to reduce the size of large particles. Additionally, flow measurement devices and wave flumes are commonly used during this phase (Pachwarya et al., 2021) . It's crucial to remove oil and grease from wastewater at this stage to mitigate its adverse effects on the subsequent treatment processes. This is typically achieved through methods such as chlorination, vacuum flotation, and aeration (Pachwarya et al., 2021) .

chunks.text: In the activated sludge process the majority of biological solids removed in the secondary sedimentation tank are recycled (returned sludge). The feedback of most of the cell yields from the sedimentation tank encourages rapid adsorption of the pollutants in the incoming settled sewage and also serves to stabilize the operation over a wide range of dilution rates and substrate concentrations imposed by fluctuations in the flow and strength of the wastewater. Secondary treatment processes can remove up to 95 per cent of the BOD and suspended solids entering the process, as well as significant amounts of heavy metals and certain organic compounds which could otherwise cause the deterioration of chemical and ecological quality of receiving waters [10, 53] . Conventional wastewater treatment usually ends with secondary treatment which cannot efficiently remove all the different compounds found in sewage and therefore treated effluents are one of the main sources of persistent micropollutants in the environment [1, 62] . For water reuse, tertiary treatment is needed to provide additional removal of contaminants such as microbial pathogens, particulates, or nutrients, and advanced treatment processes are employed when wastewater is to be reclaimed for reuse, depending on the type of use and quality requirements [49] .

chunks.text: Based on a survey on pre-treatment measures for 17 full-scale AeMBRs, the following information deserves special attention (Itokawa et al., 2008) : 1) grit chamber, coarse and fine screenings are mostly essential for MBR operation to removal grits, large suspended particles and long fibers, with fine screening (3 mm for FS membrane and 0.5-1 mm for HF membrane) installed universally; and 2) using the "by pass sieving" method, which recycles part of the suspended sludge through a sieve, achieves the further removal of unfavorable substances accumulated in the bioreactor. These means can be extended to AnMBRs minimizing the presence of undesirable substances into the bioreactor while with adequate consideration of keeping strict anaerobic environment. A recent novel concept, referred to as wastewater pre-concentration (Ansari et al., 2016) , is still under investigation, but has shown great potential to enhance bioresource recovery and energy generation efficiency (Guven et al., 2019) , accompanied by a low volumetric flow rate and process footprint (Alvarado et al., 2020) .
